evidence.title: Claude prompt caching
evidence.excerpt: By default, the cache has a 5-minute lifetime.
evidence.conditions: 5-minute writes 1.25× input; 1-hour writes 2×. Hits refresh TTL from request start. Exact prefix required. Opus 5 minimum 512; Sonnet 5 minimum 1024 tokens. Direct API; gateway behavior can differ.

evidence.title: OpenAI prompt caching
evidence.excerpt: The only supported value, `30m`, is also the default.
evidence.conditions: GPT-5.6+ minimum 1024 visible tokens; writes 1.25× input. Retention is at least 30 minutes; the forecast conservatively expires at 30 minutes, not a measured eviction guarantee.

evidence.title: Claude compaction billing
evidence.conditions: Additional sampling is billable. Use iteration usage; a summary can invalidate a prefix. Calculator conservatively rewrites all retained context. No universal quality guarantee.

evidence.title: Reasoning output and retention
evidence.conditions: Effort controls reasoning but supplies no universal tokens-per-effort multiplier. GPT-5.6 defaults to rendering available earlier reasoning; retention is explicit in this calculator. Zero extra reasoning means unspecified additional tokens, not a measured absence.

evidence.title: The Coding Agent Economy
evidence.excerpt: platform-wide cache hit rates rising from 52% to 86%
evidence.conditions: Gateway observation, May 2025–April 2026, nine agents. Claude Code: 92% cache-hit input and 84k mean prompt. Observational platform selection, not a local success experiment; do not reuse the paper’s approximate 7× cost claim as an exact tariff calculation.

evidence.title: Lost in the Middle
evidence.excerpt: multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval
evidence.conditions: 2023 models, position-sensitive retrieval and QA. Does not measure these four current models or coding-task success probabilities.

evidence.title: RULER: effective context length
evidence.conditions: Synthetic retrieval, multi-hop and aggregation, 2024 model cohort. Advertised context windows did not establish effective context length. Not a calibrated quality penalty for this forecast.

evidence.title: Context Rot
evidence.conditions: Controlled input-length variation and distractors; task complexity held constant. Model-specific degradation; not causal evidence that restarting a coding session improves success.

evidence.title: Evaluating Context Compression for AI Agents
evidence.conditions: Vendor study, three methods, four probes per compression point, six dimensions, GPT-5.2 judge. Overall scores 3.70/3.44/3.35 out of 5; these are recall/continuity scores, not task success rates. No model-specific multiplier is imported.

evidence.title: Retained orchestrator trace
evidence.conditions: July 11 2026: 33550 initial input; cache writes grew 1649 tokens across two follow-ups (824.5/turn); output 1139/3≈380. Actual gaps 577 and 500 minutes. Warm 1-minute scenario is a sensitivity assumption; raw live bus records not retained.

evidence.title: Card summary ad-hoc cohort
evidence.conditions: June 23–July 25 2026; bounded 5000-event query. Mean 22533 read, 28276 write, 9 input, 1175 output. Different role from general tasks; general-task preset is a proxy, not a representative sample. Raw ledger absent.

evidence.title: Two isolated coding runs
evidence.conditions: Sol medium: 3339 fresh + 9984 cached input, 227 output. Terra medium: 3035 fresh + 10496 cached, 137 output. N=2; neither measures per-turn growth in repeated tasks. Sol reconstruction is reused as a transparent proxy.

evidence.title: AGT-2840 operator report
evidence.conditions: N=1, September 2026 task brief; 406 fresh tokens and reported $18.24. Rounded tokens reprice to $18.23953 at Opus 5 catalogue rates. No raw run, turn count or duration supplied; cannot identify growth or typicality.

evidence.title: Forecast boundaries and free parameters
evidence.excerpt: Forecasts are not fitted task-success models.
evidence.conditions: Task counts, turns/task, within-task gaps, shared-prefix reuse, compaction sizes, success probabilities and quota conversions are explicit assumptions. Reasoning output estimates are user-owned; model and effort changes do not establish equivalent quality.

presets.title: Repeated programming tasks
presets.question: When does retaining this code base cost more than reconstructing each task?
presets.parameterNotes: N=2 isolated coding runs. Initial context, fresh reconstruction and output use the Sol run; 3339 tool tokens/turn, 4 turns/task and 12 tasks are extrapolations. Shared-prefix reuse is conditional on identical content.

presets.title: Orchestrator decisions
presets.question: How much does each later decision cost, and when does a restart or compaction repay its cost?
presets.parameterNotes: N=1 session, 3 calls. Growth rounded to 825; output rounded to 380; remaining 445 assigned to tools as an assumption. 60 warm decisions extrapolate far beyond the trace; observed gaps were 577 and 500 minutes.

presets.title: Switching topics
presets.question: What does unrelated history cost when each task could start from a short brief?
presets.parameterNotes: N=713 card-summary calls used as a workload-size proxy; N=0 measured general-topic sessions. Growth, 12 topics and identical shared prefixes are assumptions, not an observed cohort.
